question: What was the average annual growth rate of industries comprising mining, manufacturing and electricity during the post-reform period between 1991-92 and 2011- 12?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6.7%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The average annual growth rate of industries comprising **mining, manufacturing, and electricity** during the post-reform period (1991-92 to 2011-12) was recorded at **6.7%**.
 
• This growth reflects the structural changes in the Indian economy following the implementation of the **1991 economic reforms**, which included liberalization, privatization, and globalization.
 
• Among the industrial sectors, manufacturing exhibited robust growth, while mining faced challenges due to environmental and regulatory issues.
 
• The electricity sector also witnessed significant growth during this period, driven by **increased power generation capacity** and reforms in the energy sector.
 
• The higher growth rate of the industrial sector contributed significantly to India's overall GDP growth during the post-reform period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1991 Economic Reforms:**

 
 
• These reforms marked a shift from a mixed economy to a market-oriented economy in India.
 
• Key measures included **reducing import tariffs, deregulating markets, and reducing the role of public sector enterprises**.
 
• The reforms aimed to address the balance of payments crisis and boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Sector Breakdown:**
 
 
• **Mining:** Contributed significantly to raw material supply but faced challenges in sustainability and environmental compliance.
 
• **Manufacturing:** Benefited from increased foreign direct investment (FDI), technological advancements, and policy support.
 
• **Electricity:** Growth was fueled by infrastructure investments and reforms in the energy sector, such as the Electricity Act of 2003.
 
 
 
• **Electricity Act, 2003:**
 
 
• Introduced reforms to promote competition, efficiency, and private sector participation in the power sector.
 
• Facilitated the development of renewable energy and increased power generation capacity.
 
 
 
• **Impact on GDP:**
 
 
• The industrial sector contributed substantially to India’s GDP growth, averaging around **27%-30% of GDP** during this period.
 
• This growth was instrumental in reducing poverty levels and creating employment opportunities in India.
